What moves the price on a 939A2000 is the condition of the timing chain, the state of the DPF and EGR system, and whether the dual-mass flywheel has been replaced. failures.title: Alfa Romeo 939A2000 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch - The 939A2000's Most Notorious Issue
items.whatHappens: Like many Alfa Romeo diesel engines, the 939A2000 uses a timing chain that can stretch over time. The chain is located at the rear of the engine, making replacement a labour-intensive job. Symptoms include rattling on cold start-up, poor performance, and check-engine lights. If the chain jumps, valves will contact pistons, resulting in catastrophic engine failure. This is the single biggest failure point on the 1.9 JTDM.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early (rattling only), timing chain and tensioner replacement is a manageable repair (£800-£1,500). If the chain has jumped, the engine is typically beyond economical repair - a full replacement is the only option. Read our full timing chain failure guide

items.title: DPF & EGR Clogging - Urban Driving & Regeneration Issues
items.whatHappens: The 939A2000's Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) and Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) system are prone to clogging, particularly on vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys where the DPF cannot complete a regeneration cycle. Symptoms include reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and warning lights. The EGR valve can also stick due to carbon buildup.
items.repairVsReplace: DPF cleaning is a specialist job (£200-£600). EGR valve cleaning or replacement is also manageable (£200-£500). These are repairable issues and rarely require engine replacement. Read our full DPF failure guide

items.title: Dual-Mass Flywheel (DMF) Wear - Clutch Judder & Vibrations
items.whatHappens: The 939A2000's dual-mass flywheel is a known wear item, particularly on high-torque diesel engines. Symptoms include clutch judder, vibration at idle, and a rattling noise from the bellhousing when the engine is running. If the DMF fails, it can damage the starter motor and gearbox input shaft.
items.repairVsReplace: DMF replacement is a gearbox-out job (£800-£1,200) and is often done alongside a clutch replacement. This does not typically require engine replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 939A2000 was produced from 2005 to 2011, with later engines (2008+) benefiting from improved timing chain materials and revised tensioner design. However, the core vulnerabilities remain - regular oil changes (5,000-8,000 miles) with the correct 5W-40 oil are essential to protect the timing chain and turbocharger. The DPF and EGR issues are inherent to all modern diesels with urban use - regular motorway driving to allow DPF regeneration is essential.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 939A2000
variants.intro: The 939A2000 is the 1.9-litre JTDM diesel engine, producing 150 hp (110 kW). It is part of the GM/Fiat 1.9 JTDM family and is used exclusively in the Alfa Romeo 159 and Brera. It is distinguished from earlier 1.9 JTD engines by its 16-valve cylinder head and common-rail injection system. Where the code appears: - Stamped on a metal plate on the engine block (left-hand side) - On the V5C logbook under "Engine number" (the first 8 characters will read 939A2000) - Via Alfa Romeo VIN decoder Commonly confused with: - [939A6000 - LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - the 1.9 JTS petrol engine (160 hp), used in some 159 models; completely different engine, not interchangeable - [939A000 - LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - the 3.2 V6 JTS petrol engine (260 hp), used in higher-spec 159 and Brera models - [939A4000 - LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - another variant of the 1.9 JTDM with different power output

Used 8-valve cylinder heads and different injection technology - the 939A2000 introduced 16-valve heads and improved common-rail for better performance and refinement.

LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - the 2.0-litre diesel engine that replaced the 1.9 JTDM in later Alfa Romeo models. Larger displacement and improved emissions - not a straight swap with the 1.9L 939A2000.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 939A2000 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 939A2000 can make sense for lower-value 159 or Brera models where the car's value doesn't justify a recon unit. However, the timing chain and DPF are the biggest risks - only consider a used unit with documented proof of recent timing chain replacement, DPF cleaning, and regular oil service history. Without that, factor in £800-£1,500 for preventative work (timing chain, DPF cleaning).

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper 939A2000 recon is the best option for owners planning to keep their Alfa long-term. A quality recon should include: full strip and inspection, new timing chain and tensioner (critical), new injectors or full refurbishment, DPF cleaning, new gaskets and seals, and a full test. With a 12-24 month warranty, this gives you peace of mind that the engine's known weaknesses have been addressed - well worth the £800-£1,200 supply cost.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified when the original engine has suffered catastrophic failure (chain jump, DPF blockage leading to oil dilution, injector failure) and the car is a cherished keeper. An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons/rings, refreshed cylinder head, new timing chain and guides, and a full DPF/turbo overhaul. This is specialist territory and typically only makes sense for cars with strong residual value.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted Alfa Romeo diesel specialists nationwide, with 12-month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units. Link once: /services/supply-and-fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The 939A2000 sits in Alfa Romeo 159 and Brera - cars now worth £2,000-£10,000 depending on age, condition, and spec. With a reconditioned supply cost of £800-£1,200, replacement is viable on most examples. However, for a sub-£2,000 159 or Brera with high mileage and a failed engine, a used unit (£400-£700) with documented history may be the only sensible option. For cars worth under £1,500, consider breaking the car before committing to a replacement engine. Given the Alfa Romeo brand's passionate following and the 159/Brera's growing classic status, many owners choose to invest in a reconditioned engine to preserve their car.

items.question: What are the most common failures on the 939A2000 1.9 JTDM engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are timing chain stretch (causing rattling on start-up and potential chain jump), DPF and EGR clogging (particularly with urban driving), and dual-mass flywheel wear (clutch judder and vibrations). The timing chain is the single biggest failure point on the 1.9 JTDM - regular oil changes with the correct 5W-40 oil are essential to protect it. Timing chain: rattling on start-up is the early warning sign. DPF/EGR: regular motorway driving for regeneration is essential. DMF: replacement at clutch change is recommended.

items.question: How do I confirm if my car has the 939A2000 or another engine?
items.answer: Check the engine code stamped on the block (left-hand side) - it will read 939A2000 for the 1.9 JTDM diesel, or another code for petrol variants (e.g., 939A6000 for 1.9 JTS petrol). The V5C logbook also lists the full engine number, with the first 8 characters identifying the code. 939A2000: 1.9L JTDM diesel (150 hp), used in 159 & Brera. 939A6000: 1.9L JTS petrol (160 hp), different engine. 939A000: 3.2L V6 JTS petrol, different engine.
bullets: 939A2000: 1.9L JTDM diesel (150 hp), used in 159 & Brera.

items.question: How long does a 939A2000 engine typically last?
items.answer: With meticulous maintenance and early preventative work, these engines can exceed 120,000-150,000 miles. The 939A2000 is fundamentally a robust engine; the limiting factors are the timing chain, DPF/EGR system, and dual-mass flywheel. Timing chain replacement recommended at 60k-80k miles as preventative. DPF/EGR: regular motorway driving for regeneration is essential. Regular oil changes (5,000-8,000 miles) with 5W-40 oil are essential.
